answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks with slashable-stake vouching: a new identity cannot earn or transact until five established, mutually unrelated peers countersign its first outputs, each locking a stake that is slashed if the newcomer proves fake. Attackers can wander in with a thousand fresh accounts, but they cannot fabricate the endorsement web without risking real capital and accumulated history. Trust grows like a meadow from genuine work, while sybils wither in a lagoon of unverifiable claims, since peers audit random past outputs before any endorsement is issued.
